question.text: An NPO's tax exemption and donor tax-benefit status are granted under which sections of the Income Tax Act 1961?

answer.text: Section 12A/12AB (registration for tax exemption) and Section 80G (donor deduction eligibility)
Section 10(23C) only; no other sections are relevant
Section 11 (application of income) and Section 35AC (scientific research)

explanation.text: The Logic: NPO tax exemption is tied to Section 12A/12AB registration under the Income Tax Act 1961, and donor tax deduction is granted under Section 80G. These two sections together form the primary tax-benefit pair for NPOs. The Trap: Option A is wrong because Section 135 is part of the Companies Act (not the IT Act) and 115BBI deals with anonymous-donation taxation. Option C narrows the field too far by excluding 80G and 12AB. Option D mixes Section 11 (application of income) and 35AC (scientific research), neither of which is the registration/deduction pair asked. Note: Verify both the 12A/12AB registration and the 80G approval are currently valid before relying on the NPO's tax-exempt status or the donor-deduction representation in the engagement.
